what_this_is_not: R values are copied from the tracked fixture. Julia values are computed fresh by tools/true_parity_julia_receipts.jl, which repeats the computation of the cited twin test with the same inputs and settings; R was not run and is not recomputed here.

cases.quantity: tidy(fit) fixed rows, column `estimate`, 6 trait intercepts
cases.julia_source: GLLVModels.tidy(fit, Y), field estimate, as called at test/test_namespace_numeric_p1_twin_b.jl:63; fit as at test/test_namespace_numeric_p1_twin_b.jl:60
cases.tolerance_source_line: @test isapprox([r.estimate for r in tb], Float64.(t["estimate"]); atol = 1e-6, rtol = 0)
cases.note: Rank-2 Gaussian fit on the fixture data (sha256 checked; the same data as the main fit of the extract_loadings twin), R: latent(0 + trait | unit, d = 2, unique = FALSE) converged with a positive-definite Hessian; same optimum (logLik within 1e-6, asserted in the test). Rows are the six trait intercepts in trait order (R terms traitt1..traitt6, Julia beta[1..6]); the test asserts the row count and the identity link on both sides, and the numbers are compared elementwise.
